findings.description: T-001's C-1 check_method applies C-1's check text verbatim, and that text ends by requiring the checker to confirm `.agent-guild/CLAUDE.md`'s waiver description was widened. That widening is T-003's entire deliverable, and T-003 deps on T-001, so at T-001's check time it cannot exist. T-001's checker is obliged to FAIL on a requirement T-001's worker was never asked to satisfy, burning a retry and injecting a rework diagnosis that sends a sonnet worker into the exact file T-003 exists to write.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:77 ('Confirm `.agent-guild/CLAUDE.md`'s waiver description was widened to match.'); tasks/T-001.md:10-11 ('apply clause C-1's check text ... verbatim against the delivered tree'); T-001's spec excerpt (T-001.md:34-96) never names `.agent-guild/CLAUDE.md` at all; tasks/T-003.md:19 `deps: [T-001]`. Fix: scope T-001's C-1 application to the code half, naming the CLAUDE.md sentence as T-003's and checked there. Do NOT fix it by reversing the dependency -- see the T-003/deps finding.

findings.description: All four tasks check a commit subject under C-9, and no excerpt tells any worker to commit. Nothing else in the kit does either: no worker role, no task template, and neither the decompose nor the job skill mentions committing. This is not a prediction -- T-002's worker has already returned with the work uncommitted, and its checker was dispatched to read a commit subject that does not exist.
findings.evidence: check_method commit-subject clauses at tasks/T-001.md:24-25, T-002.md:13-16, T-003.md:13-15, T-004.md:27-28. `git log -1` = 92385bb (pre-job tip); `git status` = ' M .agent-guild/hooks/dispatch-guard.py'; tasks/T-002.md now reads `status: checking` with `artifacts: [.agent-guild/hooks/dispatch-guard.py]`. `grep -rn -i commit guild-core/roles/worker-*.md guild-core/workflows/decompose/SKILL.md guild-core/workflows/job/SKILL.md .agent-guild/templates/task.md` -> no matches. dispatches.log: '2026-08-11T22:48:18Z | checker-judgment | T-002 | opus'.

findings.description: CON-audit r4's C-8 minor reached the worker's excerpt but not the checker's rubric, and the worker-side mitigation does not cover the case r4 named. T-001's C-8 check_method still says only 'neutralizing its branch in a copy of the delivered code' -- the bare word r4 flagged as admitting two operations that flip different cases. Telling the worker to write both kinds of case does not close it: decisiveness is judged per case, so a checker who disables the branch (r4's neutralization Y) while examining a refuse-case still sees it not flip and reports an honest implementation as not decisive.
findings.evidence: tasks/T-001.md:21-23 (check_method C-8) against CON-audit-r4.md, C-8 minor row: 'One sentence closes it: neutralize by restoring the branch's pre-change decision for the input under test, not by disabling the branch.' That sentence appears in neither the check_method nor the excerpt. T-001.md:88-93 carries the worker-side half only ('write both kinds of case so either reading finds what it needs').

findings.description: The decomposition was put into execution while this audit was in flight, so the artifact moved under audit and the findings above now land on work already done. Two task files also changed mid-audit: T-002's and T-004's `checker` field read `checker-deterministic` when I opened them and reads `checker-judgment` now. The current values are correct (see the routing finding), but a verdict is only as good as the artifact it was derived from, and this one had to be re-derived twice.
findings.evidence: state/log/dispatches.log, consecutive rows: '2026-08-11T17:44:26 | auditor | DEC-audit | opus', '2026-08-11T17:45:45 | worker-bulk | T-002 | haiku', '2026-08-11T22:47:02Z | worker-standard | T-001 | sonnet', '2026-08-11T22:48:18Z | checker-judgment | T-002 | opus'. `.agent-guild/CLAUDE.md` puts the DEC-audit at the end of Phase 1 and building in Phase 2; unlike CON-audit, dispatch-guard does not enforce it.

findings.description: Second consequence of dispatching during the audit, and it is the issue under audit in miniature: subagent-return could not tell which agent was returning. On a Claude host SubagentStop hands the hook the PARENT's transcript, and id_from_transcript returns tool_ids[-1] -- the most recent dispatch the parent made, not the dispatch that started the returning agent. Three agents were dispatched after this auditor, so the id resolved to T-002 and the auditor branch demanded a T-002 audit verdict from an agent that never audited T-002. I refused to write it. That refusal is the same one the #100 mitigation rests on, and it is worth noting that the kit's only defense here is still an agent declining a gate message addressed to someone else. This is not confined to the auditor: tool_ids[-1] is the last dispatch the PARENT made, so EVERY subagent now returning is identified as T-002, whichever task it actually ran. T-001's worker will return into the worker branch of the same gate, be read as T-002 (status 'checking', not 'needs-check'), and be blocked on a protocol complaint about a task it never touched. Resolving this is the orchestrator's job, not a subagent's: the hand-written escape hatches in the state map belong to the orchestrator and the user by contract, so an auditor writing one for a task it was not dispatched on would be forging exactly the record this job exists to protect.
findings.evidence: Stop hook: 'Auditor finished without writing a verdict for T-002. Write .agent-guild/state/verdicts/T-002-r0.md ... before finishing.' Mechanism: _lib.py:840-841 (`if tool_ids: return tool_ids[-1]`) with the docstring at :564-566 ('Claude's SubagentStop supplies the parent transcript'); subagent-return.py:406-413 (the auditor branch, which applies the returning agent's TYPE to that id). dispatches.log shows DEC-audit at 17:44:26 followed by three later dispatches, the last being checker-judgment on T-002. spec.md:67 describes the same failure mode from the other end: an agent 'satisfying a gate message it had read, and gate messages are addressed to the orchestrator rather than to a subagent.' Predicted consequence, derived from subagent-return.py:419-437 (the worker branch) against tasks/T-002.md `status: checking`. Remedy is the phase ordering, not the gate: let an audit return before dispatching Phase 2, since overlapping dispatches make every return ambiguous. The DEC-audit verdict itself is complete and durable at this stem regardless of whether the auditor's return is ever allowed to finish.

findings.description: T-003's excerpt asks for prose saying 'what an orchestrator should do when they meet the state' but never says how the state presents to them, and never tells the worker it may read T-001's delivered code -- which it can, since T-003 runs after T-001. A worker with only this excerpt has to invent the symptom it is describing. It also pins the code comment by line number (`_lib.py:281`), which T-001 will have shifted by the time T-003 runs.
findings.evidence: tasks/T-003.md:42 ('`.agent-guild/hooks/_lib.py:281` -- the inline comment on the waiver branch') and :46-48. `_lib.py:271` (the lane-json route T-001 conjoins onto) sits ten lines above `:281`, so any added conjunct or comment moves the target. The content description ('the inline comment on the waiver branch') is recoverable; the number is not.

findings.description: Two constraints a T-001 worker would violate by default are absent. First, T-001 does not cite C-7 and its excerpt never says to leave the eleven suites green, so a regression in test_hooks.py surfaces at T-004 -- where a haiku worker gets a rework diagnosis for a sonnet-authored gate bug and burns T-004's budget on it. Second, `scripts/build-plugin.py` ships hooks from a hardcoded inventory, so a new file under `.agent-guild/hooks/` that is not added to GUILD_HOOKS silently never ships, and no suite catches it unless the file is also registered in settings.json.
findings.evidence: tasks/T-001.md:5 `clauses: [C-1, C-2, C-3, C-5, C-8, C-9]` (no C-7); constitution.md:112-113 puts all eleven suites plus build-plugin --check on T-004. scripts/build-plugin.py:109-117 (GUILD_HOOKS/OPTIONAL_HOOKS) and :460-472 (copy_hook_scripts iterates that list); the only guard, at :513-517, fires for a registered command, not for an unlisted module.

findings.description: Coverage is complete in both directions. Every Done-when bullet maps to a clause that maps to a task, all nine clauses are cited by at least one task, and no spec content falls through. The spec's contaminated-ledger observation is covered by declared non-goals rather than dropped, and the forged crossing it worries about is already outside #34's corpus by path.
findings.evidence: Done-when 1 (spec.md:87) -> C-1/C-3 -> T-001; 2 (:88) -> C-3 -> T-001; 3 (:89) -> C-2 -> T-001; 4 (:90) -> C-6 -> T-004. Citations: C-1 (T-001,T-003), C-2/C-3/C-5/C-8 (T-001), C-4 (T-002), C-6/C-7 (T-004), C-9 (all four). classify-crossings.py:113-121 globs `archive/*/tasks/*.md` and the sibling `verdicts/` dir; the forgery sits in `archive/2026-08-11-issue-100/quarantine/`, so it was never in the corpus and needs no task.

findings.description: The graph is a DAG, every referenced task exists, and T-004's deps are complete -- re-derived from what build-plugin.py actually copies rather than from the claim in T-004's excerpt. The build's inputs are `.agent-guild/hooks/` (including test_hooks.py, which T-001 edits), `.agent-guild/CLAUDE.md`, `.agent-guild/scripts|templates|schemas/`, `guild-core/roles|workflows/`, `scripts/plugin-src/`, `docs/plugin-readme.md`, and `.claude/settings.json`. This job touches the first two; T-004 deps on every task that touches either, and on the third task besides.
findings.evidence: Edges: T-001 [], T-002 [], T-003 [T-001], T-004 [T-001,T-002,T-003] -- no cycle, no dangling id. build-plugin.py:109-118 (GUILD_HOOKS includes test_hooks.py), :460-472 (copy_hook_scripts), :665-692 (assemble_project_template copies GUILD_DIR/CLAUDE.md, scripts, templates, schemas), :428-447 (sync_dogfood writes .claude/ from guild-core/). guild-core/ holds only roles/ and workflows/ -- `.agent-guild/CLAUDE.md` is a source, not a generated view, so T-003 edits the right file and T-004's rebuild cannot clobber it.

findings.description: T-001 is correctly one dispatch, and the reason is stronger than 'splitting costs something'. C-2 forbids a time-window predicate (its concurrency case is the incident run's own overlap), which leaves a dispatch-time snapshot of the verdicts directory as the only way to attribute a foreign-stem write -- and that snapshot is the same artifact C-1's 'a stem already present at dispatch is not recorded' rule requires. One data structure serves both clauses. A split would put its format on a seam neither task owns and no clause checks. Sonnet is the right tier by the routing table's own rule (clear-spec implementation judged on correctness): the seam is fixed, the outcome is pinned rather than the ordering, and volume is what the retry ladder is for.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:82 ('A verdict written concurrently by a different agent for its own task never blocks an unrelated return ... a time-window predicate would fire on innocent work') and :76 ('A stem already present when its courier was dispatched is not recorded as authorized'). Seam confirmed live: dispatch-guard.py:259 (tid), :331 (courier_lane), :368 (executor_model), :378 (retries); subagent-return.py:451-457 (the Codex read-only branch that returns 0 before any file exists) and :465 (the stem it recomputes).

findings.description: Ruling on the dependency direction: T-003 depends on T-001 is correct, keep it. Contract-first looks tempting because it would let T-001's checker apply C-1 whole -- but T-003 edits the waiver branch's inline comment in `_lib.py`, and T-001 rewrites that same branch. Contract-first would leave that comment describing a branch restructured after it was checked, with T-003 already complete and nothing re-reading it. The prose half has no dependency on T-001's implementation choices either (T-003's own excerpt forbids restating the mechanism), so contract-first buys nothing against that cost. Fix the C-1 check split instead, per the blocker above.
findings.evidence: tasks/T-003.md:42 targets `_lib.py:281`; T-001's excerpt (T-001.md:70-72) directs the worker at `_lib.py:271`/`:281` and says where the authorization conjunct goes decides whether the waiver stays reachable. Same ten-line region, two tasks. tasks/T-003.md:46-47 ('Do not restate the mechanism T-001 built; say what an orchestrator should do when they meet the state').

findings.description: Routing is correct as the files now stand. Every task citing both a script clause and a rubric clause carries checker-judgment, which is the only assignment that works: checker-deterministic is defined as zero-discretion and its verdict rule is exit codes only, so a rubric entry in its check_method would return blocked, while checker-judgment carries Bash and can run the scripts. T-002's and T-004's executors are correctly worker-bulk (a one-line stamp change; a build re-run), and T-003's worker-craft/opus is justified rather than over-tiered -- the orchestrator contract is prose every agent reads as instructions each session, which is the routing table's taste-work case.
findings.evidence: guild-core/roles/checker-deterministic.md:1 ('zero discretion ... You do not interpret, improve, or judge') and its verdict rule ('Any command missing, crashing, or exiting 3 -> blocked'); .claude/agents/checker-judgment.md:5 `tools: Read, Bash, Write, Grep, Glob`. Mixed-form tasks: T-001 (C-3 script + five rubrics), T-002 (C-4 script + C-9 rubric), T-004 (C-6/C-7 scripts + C-9 rubric) -- all three now checker-judgment. Note both T-002 and T-004 read checker-deterministic at the start of this audit; see the process finding.

findings.description: The third r4 minor reached the tasks intact. T-003 names all three narrow paraphrases of the waiver, requires them to agree, and all three line references resolve on the current tree. A fourth paraphrase exists in `test_hooks.py` and a fifth in `_lib.py`'s docstring; neither is a defect -- the docstring's is scope-neutral, and no clause governs a stale test comment.
findings.evidence: tasks/T-003.md:40-42 names CLAUDE.md:87, CLAUDE.md:125, _lib.py:281. Verified: CLAUDE.md:87 ('your waiver, for a host that refused the dispatch outright'), CLAUDE.md:125 ('the waiver, for a lane that never got as far as a courier at all'), _lib.py:281 ('route 4: the orchestrator's record that a host refused the dispatch outright (e.g. #94)'). The other two: test_hooks.py:986 (narrow, ungoverned) and _lib.py:241 ('an orchestrator waiver', which claims no scope).

findings.description: Ruling on the second r4 minor -- the header saying 'Four things changed' when five did: it needed no task, and none was owed. That sentence lives in an HTML comment in the constitution's own header, not in a clause; no deliverable ships it, no check reads it, and no worker sees it. It is orchestrator-owned state the write-guard does not block, so correcting the count in place costs one word and requires no re-audit. Leaving it costs only that a later reader reconstructing r4 from the header would miss the C-2 edit.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:32 ('Four things changed') against the five edits r4 actually made; the fifth is C-2's two-channel sentence at constitution.md:82, absent from the bullet list at :34-49. No task cites the header, and the constitution is not a build input to scripts/build-plugin.py.
